“I have become a hybrid surgeon.”

Oral Surgery Mastery
Periodontal Principles
Prosthodontic Principles

“Today, successful implantology requires a hybrid approach. A practitioner must be as skilled in the macro-stability of bone, the surgeon’s traditional wheelhouse, as they are in the microbiology and esthetics of the gingival margin, historically the periodontist’s domain. As a hybrid surgeon, I understand implant dentistry from A to Z, from diagnosis and planning to surgery, tissue management, restoration, and long-term success. This allows our restorative colleagues to deliver restorations that are aesthetically compatible, functionally sound, anatomically precise, and biologically stable.”

02

What I treatMy core competence

Extractions & Wisdom Teeth

Minimally-invasive techniques, micro incisions, micro flaps, socket shield, partial extraction therapies.

Dental Implants

Digitally-driven planning and guided placement. Single to multiple implants.

Full Arch

Fixed and removable, FP1, FP2, and FP3. Immediate load, staged therapies.

Bone & Soft Tissue Grafting

Socket grafts, horizontal and vertical augmentations, sinus lift, vestibuloplasty, attached gingiva development.

Failing Implants

Reverse torque explantation and revision therapies.

Severe Bone Atrophy

KLS IPS patient-specific implants, zygomatic and pterygoid implants.

Orthodontic & Pediatric

Selective extractions, canine exposures, orthognathic surgery.

Oral Pathology

Biopsies, jaw cysts, oral medicine.

Emergencies

Emergency extractions, infection, and trauma. Always seen on the same day.

04

Working with specialistsPartners on multidisciplinary cases, never a competition.

“Each specialty has different needs. Here is what I do for each.”

Periodontists

  • Complex implant complications and revision therapy
  • Advanced bone augmentation
  • Severe atrophy, where conventional grafting and implants may not be possible: KLS IPS, zygomatic and pterygoid implants

Orthodontists

  • Canine exposures
  • Exposure of impacted teeth and removal of supernumerary teeth for orthodontic eruption
  • Wisdom teeth extractions

Pediatric Dentists

  • Extraction of primary teeth
  • Canine exposures
  • Wisdom teeth extractions

Endodontists

  • Teeth that cannot be saved: atraumatic extraction, socket grafting and implant site planning
  • Periapical cysts: excision and guided bone regeneration of the defect
  • Resorption cases: the surgical side, alongside endodontic and restorative care
